cues.text: Well, we have this school excursion planned, but when exactly is it? Is it this Tuesday or Wednesday?
cues.speaker: Andrew

cues.text: Well it can’t be Tuesday, with the English tests taking place.
cues.speaker: Katie

cues.text: Ah, right. Not Tuesday, but Wednesday.
cues.speaker: Andrew

cues.text: That’s right - all day Wednesday - taking a bus outside the city.
cues.speaker: Katie

cues.text: And where are we going?
cues.speaker: Andrew

cues.text: Ah, last month we went to Arthur Island, so this time we’re going to the... Animal Park.
cues.speaker: Katie

cues.text: Arthur Island was okay, but it was too cold. Let’s hope the weather for this week’s excursion is better. I don’t suppose animals care about bad weather, but I certainly do. Have you heard the forecast?
cues.speaker: Andrew

cues.text: Yes, and it’s not too bad. Basically, they’re saying Monday will be sunny.
cues.speaker: Katie

cues.text: Good...
cues.speaker: Andrew

cues.text: But then the weather will change.
cues.speaker: Katie

cues.text: Not so good.
cues.speaker: Andrew

cues.text: Yes, Tuesday we’ll have some showers, but by Wednesday, the day of our excursion, it will be... well, their words are ‘ cold and cloudy’.
cues.speaker: Katie

cues.text: Cold and cloudy. Well, as long as it isn’t ‘wet and rainy’, I’m happy enough. We won’t need umbrellas, just warm clothing. And what time will we get there?
cues.speaker: Andrew

cues.text: Let’s see. The bus picks us up at 8.30 am, and then it’s an hour and a half on the road, so we arrive at 10 am... sorry, with the 15 minutes break, that will actually be 10.15 am.
cues.speaker: Katie

cues.text: That’s early enough. Then all our students can see the animals, have their fun, and do whatever they want to do.
cues.speaker: Andrew

cues.text: Well, one fun event planned that day is ‘ Birds of Prey’.
cues.speaker: Katie

cues.text: What’s that?
cues.speaker: Andrew

cues.text: That’s when they bring out several birds of prey: eagles, falcons, kites, those sorts of birds, and throw pieces of meat into the air, and the birds swoop down and eat them. It’s quite impressive.
cues.speaker: Katie

cues.text: Sounds great. ‘Birds of Prey’. Are there any other activities?
cues.speaker: Andrew

cues.text: There’s a catered lunch, at the park restaurant. We’ve already paid for that, and in the afternoon there’s... well, I had a choice between the ‘Reptile Display’ and the ‘Koala Handling’. In the reptile display, the students can handle live pythons and various other snakes.
cues.speaker: Katie

cues.text: Surely they’d rather hold koalas?
cues.speaker: Andrew

cues.text: I’m sure, but the koalas can’t be handled unless the weather’s sunny, and given the forecast, I thought it better to choose the reptile display.
cues.speaker: Katie

cues.text: Ummm, that’s a shame. These Asian students would love the ‘Koala Handling’.
cues.speaker: Andrew

cues.text: Yes, I know, but we can’t control the weather.
cues.speaker: Katie

cues.text: And, then we get back. What time will that be?
cues.speaker: Andrew

cues.text: We leave the park at 4.30, but then we face traffic, so wo won't get back until well after 6pm. It will most likely be 6.30. But that’s better than the last trip: we didn’t get home until 8.30 that time.
cues.speaker: Katie

cues.text: Yes, that was a bit too late, wasn’t it?
cues.speaker: Andrew

cues.text: Andrew, I understand you’ve been doing some research regarding the breakdown, by nationality of our student body. That must have produced some interesting results.
cues.speaker: Katie

cues.text: You’re right. I got some statistics from head office.
cues.speaker: Andrew

cues.text: I would imagine that most of our students are either Japanese or Chinese.
cues.speaker: Katie

cues.text: You imagine right. But it’s the Chinese who constitute the majority , but only just. I had thought Koreans might be second, but it’s actually the Japanese, quite close behind. It’s somewhat surprising, but obviously all those Study Tours that our university markets in Japan are bringing in students.
cues.speaker: Andrew

cues.text: What’s the breakdown exactly?
cues.speaker: Katie

cues.text: Japanese are a quarter of the whole, which is considerable. Last year they were only 16%, so that market has grown nicely. Ah, the only other proportions of some weight are the Indonesians and Koreans - about the same. Indonesians at 15%, and... ah... the Koreans are a little higher -not like last year when they were less than 10%.
cues.speaker: Andrew

cues.text: I thought we’d have more Indonesians than Koreans?
cues.speaker: Katie

cues.text: Well, as I said, they’re about the same - just like the Saudi and Thai student numbers, almost the same also - both just under 10.
cues.speaker: Andrew

cues.text: Which one is bigger?
cues.speaker: Katie

cues.text: Ah, Thai students number just a fraction more. As for the other nationalities, collectively they’re only 3%, so it wasn’t worth giving each of them a separate category. I just grouped them under ‘other’ - that’s Vietnamese, South American, a couple of Russians, and so on.
cues.speaker: Andrew
